'''Christiane Tretter''' is a German mathematician and mathematical physicist who works as a professor in the Mathematical Institute (MAI) of the [[University of Bern]] in Switzerland, and as co-director of the institute.{{r|mai}} Her research area in applied analysis includes, in particular, [[spectral theory]] and [[differential operator]]s.

==Education and career==
Tretter studied mathematics, with a minor in physics, at the [[University of Regensburg]], earning a [[diplom]]a in 1989, a Ph.D. in 1992, and a [[habilitation]] in 1998. Her doctoral dissertation, ''Asymptotische Randbedingungen für Entwicklungssätze bei Randeigenwertproblemen zu <math>N(y) = \lambda P(y)</math> mit <math>\lambda</math>-abhängigen Randbedingungen'', was supervised by Reinhard Mennicken.{{r|mg}}

She became a lecturer at the [[University of Leicester]] in 2000, moved to the [[University of Bremen]] as a professor in 2002, and took her present position as full professor at the [[University of Bern]] in 2006.

Since 2008 she has been editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[Integral Equations and Operator Theory]]''.{{r|ieot}}. Having served as vice-president of the [[Swiss Mathematical Society, SMS]], in 2024/25,  she was elected president of SMS in 2026.{{r|SMS}}

==Books==
Tretter is the author of two mathematical monographs, ''Spectral Theory of Block Operator Matrices and Applications'' (2008){{r|stbom}} and ''On Lambda-Nonlinear-Boundary-Eigenvalue-Problems'' (1993),{{r|lnbep}} and of two textbooks in analysis{{r|an1}}{{r|an2}}.

==Recognition==
Tretter was awarded the [[Richard von Mises Prize]] of the [[Gesellschaft für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik, GAMM]], in 1995.{{r|mises}} She became honorary member of the [[Swedish Mathematical Society]] in 2025{{r|swedms}}.
